seoTitle.en: Love Personality Test: 24 Choices & Full Results

description.en: Take 24 paired choices about expression, response, space and repair. Read all 15 full public result guides, including ties. Free, with no signup.
description.zh: 通过24道原创二选一题，回看表达、回应、靠近与空间、分歧修复四种互动入口。免费作答，15种含并列结果均有完整公开说明，无需注册。

introduction.en: How do you tend to open a relationship conversation: put something into words, check a response, adjust space or consider a repair step? This original FermatMind questionnaire compares your choices across four entries. It records this attempt rather than a fixed love type. All single and tied explanations are public, so you can read them before deciding to answer.
introduction.zh: 想表达在意、回应对方、调整联系节奏或面对分歧时，你更自然从哪里开始？这份费马原创题本用24道成对选择，回看清楚表达、留意回应、调节靠近与空间、参与分歧修复四个入口。结果记录本次回答，不是固定恋爱人格；15种单独或并列说明都可先读。

instructions.en: For each pair, choose the response closer to your current, more natural choice. Use experiences you are comfortable reflecting on; neither option is a correct answer. Complete all 24 for raw counts and a full explanation. If neither option fits or this topic is not useful, you can stop. No partner’s answers, contact details or private messages are needed.
instructions.zh: 每题比较两种做法，选择当前更接近自己、更自然的一项，可以回看你愿意观察的关系经历。两项没有正确答案，完整答完24题后才显示原始次数与完整说明；两项都不适用或不想继续时，可以结束。无需伴侣作答、联系方式或私人聊天记录。

description.en: Read Clear Expression in this original Love Personality Test: raw choice counts, request examples, timing, listening and the limits of a leading count.
description.zh: 完整阅读恋爱人格测试“清楚表达”的原始选择次数、具体请求与对话例子、时机与倾听的取舍；次数最多不代表更会沟通或伴侣更理解你。

scoreReading.en: Each chosen option adds one count to its direction. Each of the four directions appears in 12 comparisons. Clear Expression has the highest count in this attempt. This is an internal comparison, not a population rank, accuracy rate, intensity or percentile.
scoreReading.zh: 计分方式：每道题都是两个选项的二选一，你选中的方向得 1 次；四个方向各参与 12 次比较。本次清楚表达次数最多。这个数字只在本次作答内部成立，不是人群排名、准确率、浓度或百分位。

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression is FermatMind’s name for an entry into interaction: making observations, feelings, needs, boundaries and arrangements available for discussion. The label does not establish extraversion, communication skill or emotional intelligence, and it cannot tell you how another person will understand or answer.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达是费马测试自建的记忆符号，标记一种互动入口：把观察、感受、需要、边界和安排放到对话中，便于双方核对。它不等同外向、沟通能力或情商，也不保证对方如何理解或回应。

title.zh: 本次题目中的具体观察

paragraphs.en: The relevant choices include naming what matters to you, explaining the personal meaning of something affecting both people, making a specific request for support and describing a change you noticed. Their shared feature is putting information into the conversation where both people can check it. The count records your selections rather than proving these actions occurred or worked.
paragraphs.zh: 想让对方知道你的在意时，你倾向把感受和需要直接说出来；遇到影响彼此的事，你先说明它对你的意义；需要支持时，你提出具体请求；关系气氛变化时，你先说出自己注意到的变化。这些选择共同指向：先把可核对的信息放到对话中。

paragraphs.en: When you want someone to know you care, you select expressing your feelings and needs.
paragraphs.zh: 想让对方知道自己的在意时，选择把感受和需要说清楚。

paragraphs.en: When something affects both people, you select directly explaining its meaning for you.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到影响彼此的事时，选择直接说明它对自己的意义。

paragraphs.en: When you need support, you select a request specific enough to answer.
paragraphs.zh: 需要支持时，选择提出一个具体、可回应的请求。

paragraphs.en: When something important is on your mind, you select explaining sooner rather than waiting for a different moment.
paragraphs.zh: 心里有重要内容时，选择尽早说清楚，而不是等时机。

title.zh: 表达与回应的具体表现

paragraphs.en: In this bank, you more often selected first explaining an observation, need or arrangement. A question about your action affecting someone concerns describing that impact; it does not score responsibility or communication ability. Understanding, acceptance and a response still depend on both people’s wishes, timing, information and actual feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 本次选择显示，你较常选中先说明观察、需要或安排的入口。自己的做法影响到对方时，题目观察的是说明具体影响，不是责任高低或沟通能力。对方是否理解、接受或回应，仍要看双方意愿、时机、信息和实际反馈。

paragraphs.en: Compare a familiar relationship with a less familiar one: do you put the same things into words?
paragraphs.zh: 可以核对：面对熟悉和不熟悉的关系对象时，你的表达方式有没有变化？

paragraphs.en: Under pressure, you might become briefer or need to explain more fully. A specific recollection can help you check which happened.
paragraphs.zh: 情绪或压力增加时，你可能说得更简短，也可能更需要说完整；请用具体经历判断。

paragraphs.en: If the other person does not want to continue, you might wait or leave one necessary piece of information. The count cannot determine your usual choice.
paragraphs.zh: 对方暂时不愿继续时，你可能等待，也可能先留下一句必要信息；哪种更常见需回看实际情境。

paragraphs.en: A different relationship stage or more serious event may call for a different response. Check an experience rather than assuming the label will persist.
paragraphs.zh: 关系阶段或事件严重程度变化后，这个入口是否仍常见，需要通过经历核对。

title.en: When this entry may be useful

paragraphs.en: Expressing information creates something observable to check together. Whether it helps depends on explicit feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 这种做法提供一个可观察的信息核对入口；是否有用要看对方的明确反馈。

paragraphs.en: A specific request can clarify what you are asking for; it cannot guarantee acceptance or a reply.
paragraphs.zh: 具体请求可以用来标出你在请求什么；它不保证对方接受或回应。

paragraphs.en: When both people want to talk, stating a view can provide a starting point. Assess progress through what actually follows.
paragraphs.zh: 当双方愿意继续交流时，把看法放到桌面上可作为讨论的一个起点；实际进展需要回看后续发生了什么。

paragraphs.en: After a boundary or arrangement is expressed, you can check whether both people understood the same thing without presuming agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 边界和安排被说出后，可以检查双方对同一句话的理解是否一致；不预设检查结果。

paragraphs.en: Check the timing: did the situation allow both people to participate, or was one person doing all the talking?
paragraphs.zh: 可以检查：开口的时机是否允许双方继续，还是只有一方在输出？

paragraphs.en: Revisit a conversation after stating your need. Was there room for the other person to express theirs?
paragraphs.zh: 回看一次具体对话：你说完自己的需要后，有没有留出对方表达的空间？

paragraphs.en: If an explanation was heard as a lecture, ask what each person needed at that moment rather than inventing the cause.
paragraphs.zh: 如果完整说明被对方理解为讲道理，可以核对当时双方分别需要什么，而不预设原因。

paragraphs.en: For example, you say what support would help during a tiring week instead of leaving a sigh to carry the message.
paragraphs.zh: 想让对方知道你最近很累时，你直接说出需要什么支持，而不是只叹气。

paragraphs.en: When weekend plans differ, you explain your priority and then ask how the other person sees it.
paragraphs.zh: 对周末安排有不同想法，你说明自己的优先顺序，再问对方怎么看。

paragraphs.en: After a small misunderstanding, you restate your intended meaning instead of waiting for a question. These are examples to compare, not predictions about you.
paragraphs.zh: 一次小误会发生后，你重新说明原本的意思，而不是等对方来问。

paragraphs.en: Before opening a topic, ask whether the other person has capacity to listen now.
paragraphs.zh: 下次开口前，先问一句：对方现在有余量听吗？

paragraphs.en: After your part, leave an opening such as, “How is it on your side?”
paragraphs.zh: 说完自己的部分后，补一句：你那边是什么感受？

paragraphs.en: Try one concise point, then ask whether they want the fuller explanation. You may draft it privately rather than try it on someone.
paragraphs.zh: 试着把一个完整说明拆成两步：先给一句结论，再问要不要展开。

paragraphs.en: Can you recall explaining clearly but receiving a different response from the one you expected?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次，你说得很清楚，但对方的实际回应与你预期不同？

paragraphs.en: What stopped you the last time you wanted to say something and did not?
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次你想说但没说的时刻，是什么拦住了你？

paragraphs.en: When you kept only the most important sentence, what actually happened next?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你只留最重要的一句，后续实际发生了什么？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: The count does not establish greater extraversion or communication skill.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更外向或更会沟通。

paragraphs.en: It does not establish greater honesty, maturity or emotional intelligence.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更坦诚、更成熟或情商更高。

paragraphs.en: It guarantees neither fewer misunderstandings nor another person’s understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 不能保证减少误会，也不能保证对方更理解你。

paragraphs.en: It measures neither partner fit, relationship quality nor its outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示伴侣适配、关系质量或关系结局。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean you express yourself this way in every relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你在所有关系里都这样表达。

paragraphs.en: This interpretation concerns relative choices in these 24 questions. Responses can vary with the person, familiarity, current pressure and the seriousness of an event. A lower count does not mean being unable to love, immature or less capable.

summary.zh: 回答这 24 题时，你先听、先核对、先看对方当下状态这类选项被你选中的次数最多。

title.en: Attuned Response: Love Personality Test Result
title.zh: 留意回应：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Read Attuned Response in the Love Personality Test: checking meaning, listening, your own needs and why counts cannot reveal another person’s feelings.
description.zh: 完整阅读恋爱人格测试“留意回应”：如何核对意思、听见具体需要，也说出自己的部分；自报次数不能读出对方感受或证明同理心。

scoreReading.en: The chosen direction receives one count per question, and each direction appears 12 times. Attuned Response is highest in this attempt. Counts compare these choices only; they are not population positions, accuracy, intensity or percentiles.
scoreReading.zh: 得分规则：每道题选中的方向记 1 次，四个方向各出场 12 次。这次留意回应排在第一。这个次数只对本次作答有意义——它不是人群排名，不是准确率，也不代表浓度或百分位。

paragraphs.en: Attuned Response is FermatMind’s name for listening and checking what someone is expressing, noticing whether they want to continue, and adjusting a response using observable information. It does not establish kindness, consideration or empathy. A quiet face or a pause still needs interpretation through direct feedback rather than presumed mind-reading.
paragraphs.zh: 留意回应是费马测试自建的记忆符号，标记一种互动入口：倾听并核对对方正在表达什么，留意对方是否愿意继续交流，根据当下可观察的信号调整回应。它不等同善良、体贴或有同理心。

title.zh: 本次题目中的具体观察

paragraphs.en: Your selections more often favoured hearing someone out, checking a meaning or asking whether the moment suits continued conversation. In the stress example, the choice concerns asking whether listening or help with options is wanted. It records an approach chosen in this bank, rather than how considerate you are or how accurately you understand feelings.
paragraphs.zh: 本次题组中，你较常选中先听、先核对、先看对方当下是否愿意继续的入口。对方分享压力时，题目观察的是先确认对方希望被倾听还是一起想办法。这反映的是本次作答入口，不是体贴程度或读心能力。

paragraphs.en: When someone is temporarily quiet, you select checking whether they want to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 对方暂时沉默时，选择先确认对方是否愿意继续。

paragraphs.en: When someone shares stress, you select checking whether listening or thinking through options is wanted.
paragraphs.zh: 对方分享压力时，选择先确认对方希望被倾听还是一起想办法。

paragraphs.en: When discussion stalls, you select checking which part of the message has not been heard.
paragraphs.zh: 讨论不顺时，选择核对哪句话还没有被听见。

paragraphs.en: When a mood changes, you select asking whether the person wants to speak now.
paragraphs.zh: 对方情绪有变化时，选择先询问现在是否想说。

title.zh: 表达与回应的具体表现

paragraphs.en: Before responding, the selected entry gives attention to what seems to matter to the other person. In a stalled conversation it checks unheard points; after an argument it asks whether anything remains to add. Observable information and an explicit answer can guide a response. The count cannot establish what someone meant without that check.
paragraphs.zh: 回应前你倾向先理解对方最在意的部分。讨论不顺时，你留意哪些话还没被听见；一次争执结束后，你问对方还有什么需要补充。你调整回应的依据来自现场可观察的信号，而不是预设的脚本。

paragraphs.en: Compare a calm moment and a tired one: did the way you checked the desired response change?
paragraphs.zh: 可以核对：对方平静或疲惫时，你核对回应方式的做法有没有变化？

paragraphs.en: With familiar and unfamiliar people, you might rely on different signals or ask directly in both cases. Use recollections to check.
paragraphs.zh: 面对熟悉或不熟悉的人，你可能依据不同信号，也可能都会直接询问；请以经历判断。

paragraphs.en: When your own pressure rises, noticing signals may be harder or you may slow down more. This change was not measured.
paragraphs.zh: 自己的压力增加时，你可能更难留意信号，也可能更会放慢核对；题目未测量这个变化。

paragraphs.en: If a quick answer is necessary, you might offer a provisional response or ask first. The result does not decide the sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 必须快速表态时，你是先给临时回应还是先询问，需用具体情境核对。

title.en: When this entry may be useful

paragraphs.en: This entry offers a way to check observable signals; it does not reveal something the other person has not said.
paragraphs.zh: 这种做法提供一个核对可观察信号的入口，不代表你已经知道对方没说出的内容。

paragraphs.en: Asking whether listening or help is wanted gives you a checkpoint for choosing a response. Explicit feedback decides whether it fits.
paragraphs.zh: 先询问对方想被倾听还是一起想办法，可作为选择回应方式的检查点；是否合适以对方的明确反馈为准。

paragraphs.en: If someone does not want to continue, asking whether a pause would help is one possibility, not a guarantee of a particular feeling.
paragraphs.zh: 当对方暂时不愿继续时，询问是否需要停顿可以作为一个尝试；它不保证对方的感受或反应。

paragraphs.en: When a discussion is difficult, compare what happened after the check without assuming it improved the conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 讨论不顺时，可以回看核对之后实际发生了什么，而不预设对话效果。

paragraphs.en: While noticing another person’s signals, check whether your own needs were also expressed.
paragraphs.zh: 可以检查：持续留意对方信号时，你自己的需要是否也被说出来？

paragraphs.en: When someone was silent, which part of your interpretation came from observable information and which part was a guess?
paragraphs.zh: 对方沉默时，你的判断来自可观察信号还是猜测？可以通过直接询问核对。

paragraphs.en: Revisit a conversation in which you followed someone’s pace. Did you also make your own direction clear?
paragraphs.zh: 回看一次跟随对方节奏的对话：你是否也表达了自己的方向？

paragraphs.en: For example, when someone comes home unusually quiet, you ask whether the day was tiring before opening your own topic.
paragraphs.zh: 对方下班后话变少，你先问今天是不是很累，而不是直接说自己的事。

paragraphs.en: If a discussion changes atmosphere, you check whether a particular statement was misunderstood.
paragraphs.zh: 讨论到一半气氛不对，你先问对方刚才那句话是不是被误解了。

paragraphs.en: When someone describes a frustration, you ask whether they want suggestions or simply someone to listen. These scenes illustrate choices, not a verified ability to read them.
paragraphs.zh: 对方说起一件烦心事，你先确认对方想要的是建议还是只想被倾听。

paragraphs.en: After responding, add one of your own needs or views.
paragraphs.zh: 下次回应完对方后，补一句自己的需要或看法。

paragraphs.en: When a signal is unclear, ask rather than turn a guess into a fact.
paragraphs.zh: 当你不确定信号时，直接问，而不是猜。

paragraphs.en: Choose an ordinary moment to describe your own state before asking about theirs. A private draft is enough if you prefer not to start a conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 每天挑一次，先说出自己的状态，再问对方。

paragraphs.en: Have you paid so much attention to signals that you left out what you wanted to say?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次，你太在意对方的信号，反而没顾上自己想说什么？

paragraphs.en: When judging someone’s state, what was observed and what was inferred?
paragraphs.zh: 你判断对方状态时，依据的是信号，还是自己的猜测？

paragraphs.en: When you state your need first, what response have you actually seen?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你先说出自己的需要，对方通常是什么反应？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: This does not establish greater kindness, consideration or empathy.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更善良、更体贴或更有同理心。

paragraphs.en: It does not establish mind-reading or an ability to heal someone.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你能看穿对方情绪，也不能疗愈对方。

paragraphs.en: It does not make you responsible for another person’s emotions.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你要为对方的情绪负责。

paragraphs.en: It does not prove other people experience you as warm or reliable.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示别人一定觉得你温暖可靠。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean this is your response in every relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你在所有关系里都这样回应。

paragraphs.en: This interpretation concerns relative choices in these 24 questions. Responses can vary with the person, familiarity, current pressure and the seriousness of an event. A lower count does not mean being unable to love, immature or less capable.
paragraphs.zh: 这里只解释本次 24 题里你相对更常选择的方向。行为会随关系对象、熟悉程度、当下压力和事件严重程度变化；较低方向不表示不会爱、不成熟或能力不足。

headline.en: Space Regulation received the most choices in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次题组中，调节靠近与空间被选中的次数最多

summary.en: You more often chose adjusting contact, leaving space or attending to timing across these 24 comparisons.
summary.zh: 整份问卷里，你更常选的是先调整联系强度、先留出空间、先看时机的那些选项。

title.en: Space Regulation: Love Personality Test Result
title.zh: 调节靠近与空间：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Read Space Regulation in the Love Personality Test: contact rhythm, pauses, return arrangements and why a choice count does not establish attachment style.
description.zh: 完整阅读恋爱人格测试“调节靠近与空间”：联系节奏、暂停与重新联系的具体例子；本次选择次数不判定依恋类型或亲密能力。

scoreReading.en: A choice adds one count to its direction. Each of the four directions participates in 12 comparisons. Space Regulation is highest this time. This is relative to this attempt, not a population position, percentile, accuracy rate or intensity.
scoreReading.zh: 怎么计分：二选一里你选谁，谁就记 1 次；四个方向各被比较 12 次。本次调节靠近与空间次数最高。这个数字不能拿出去当人群位置或百分位看，也不是准确率或浓度，只是本次作答的相对结果。

paragraphs.en: Space Regulation is FermatMind’s label for an interaction entry that adjusts contact intensity and attends to possible pauses, time alone or reconnection. It does not establish avoidant attachment, coldness or fear of intimacy. The question is which offered action you selected, rather than why you chose it or how someone else experienced the distance.
paragraphs.zh: 调节靠近与空间是费马测试自建的记忆符号，标记一种互动入口：调整联系强度，识别需要暂停、独处或重新连接的时机。它不等同回避型依恋、冷漠或害怕亲密。

title.zh: 本次题目中的具体观察

paragraphs.en: Relevant choices include leaving room to adjust increased contact, changing the rhythm of time together and alone, first making space when solitude is needed, and pausing a heated conversation. Their shared focus is timing and interaction intensity. Selecting them does not diagnose attachment or establish a fixed personality.
paragraphs.zh: 想增加联系时，你倾向先为彼此保留可调整的空间；对安排有不同想法，你先调整靠近与独处的节奏；需要独处时，你先留出空间；争执升温时，题目观察的是先暂停当前对话。这些选择共同指向交流强度与时机的调整，不代表回避型依恋或固定人格。

paragraphs.en: When you want more contact, you select first keeping room for adjustment.
paragraphs.zh: 想增加联系时，选择先为彼此保留可调整的空间。

paragraphs.en: When you need time alone, you select making space before deciding when to reconnect from your actual state.
paragraphs.zh: 需要独处时，选择先留出空间，再根据实际状态决定何时联系。

paragraphs.en: When an argument heats up, you select pausing that conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 争执升温时，选择先暂停当前对话。

paragraphs.en: When both people are tired, you select reducing the intensity of interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 双方都很疲惫时，选择先降低互动强度。

title.zh: 表达与回应的具体表现

paragraphs.en: This attempt more often favoured reducing intensity, leaving pauses or adjusting the contact rhythm. Whether you reconnect after a pause is not directly established by these items. Describing a possible return time is an action to consider, whose use depends on willingness, timing, information and feedback; it is not a result-derived prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 本次选择显示，你较常把降低交流强度、留出停顿或调整联系节奏作为入口。暂停后是否重新联系不由题目直接测得；‘说明何时再联系’只是可尝试的行动，效果取决于双方意愿、时机、信息和实际反馈。

paragraphs.en: Pressure might increase your wish for space or your wish for contact. Check a specific experience.
paragraphs.zh: 压力增加时，你可能更想留空间，也可能更想靠近；请以具体经历判断。

paragraphs.en: Do you describe your need for space differently with familiar and less familiar people?
paragraphs.zh: 面对熟悉和不熟悉的关系对象时，你说明空间需要的方式有没有变化？

paragraphs.en: When someone explicitly asks for company, you might keep your arrangement or adjust it. The questionnaire does not predict which.
paragraphs.zh: 对方表达希望陪伴时，你可能保留原有节奏，也可能调整安排；题目没有预测哪种会发生。

paragraphs.en: Changes in life or relationship stage may change the entry you use. An actual recollection is more informative than treating the label as permanent.
paragraphs.zh: 生活阶段或关系阶段变化后，这个入口是否仍常见，需要通过实际经历核对。

title.en: When this entry may be useful

paragraphs.en: A pause is one possible way to adjust intensity during rising conflict, subject to safety and explicit feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 争执升温时，暂停可以作为调整交流强度的一个尝试；是否适用要看安全条件和双方的明确反馈。

paragraphs.en: Noticing your available capacity gives you information for deciding whether to continue or stop.
paragraphs.zh: 留意自己当下的余量，可作为决定是继续还是停顿的一个检查点。

paragraphs.en: Describing a possible reconnection arrangement allows a check of what a pause means to each person; it does not promise the plan will happen.
paragraphs.zh: 暂停时说明可能的重新联系安排，可以用来核对双方对暂停的理解；不保证后续一定如期发生。

paragraphs.en: Making space is an observable action, from which another person’s feelings cannot be inferred.
paragraphs.zh: 给出空间是一个可观察的行动入口，不能由此推断对方的感受。

paragraphs.en: After a pause, ask if your understandings of the next step differ rather than assume what someone made of the silence.
paragraphs.zh: 暂停后如果双方对后续安排的理解不同，可以用明确询问核对，不预设对方如何解读。

paragraphs.en: While adjusting your pace, check the need the other person actually expressed.
paragraphs.zh: 可以回看：调整自己节奏时，对方当下明确表达的需要是什么？

paragraphs.en: If distance keeps changing, look for information both people can check about the contact rhythm.
paragraphs.zh: 如果靠近与空间反复调整，可以检查双方是否对联系节奏有可核对的信息。

paragraphs.en: For example, during an increasingly heated discussion you propose a ten-minute pause and, if both agree, a time to return.
paragraphs.zh: 一次讨论越来越激烈，你提出先停十分钟，约好回来继续。

paragraphs.en: In a busy week, you describe needing two evenings alone and a possible Friday reconnection.
paragraphs.zh: 这周事情很多，你直接告诉对方需要两晚独处时间，并说好周五再联系。

paragraphs.en: After several days of frequent contact, you discuss a frequency each person is willing to accept. These examples are possible arrangements, not a universally suitable schedule.
paragraphs.zh: 对方连续几天找你，你先商量一个双方都能接受的联系频率。

paragraphs.en: If a pause is wanted and safe, include a possible return arrangement when describing it.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想暂停时，把回来的时间一起说出来。

paragraphs.en: In an ordinary moment when you do not need space, consider whether you want to initiate contact.
paragraphs.zh: 试着在不需要空间的时候，主动靠近一次。

paragraphs.en: Before deciding that space is wanted, ask whether the other person would prefer space or company. Their request does not remove your own right to stop.
paragraphs.zh: 暂停前先问一句：对方现在需要的是空间，还是陪伴？

paragraphs.en: When did you last choose to move closer or initiate contact?
paragraphs.zh: 你上一次主动靠近对方，是什么时候？

paragraphs.en: In a particular pause, were you seeking time alone, avoiding a difficult topic, or doing something else?
paragraphs.zh: 你留空间的时候，是真的需要独处，还是在避免一次难谈的对话？

paragraphs.en: When someone else needed space, what information helped you recognise that need?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方也需要空间，你能认出那个信号吗？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: It does not establish avoidant attachment or fear of intimacy.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你是回避型依恋或害怕亲密。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean being cold, caring less or undervaluing a relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你冷漠、不够爱或不重视关系。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean independence removes every need for other people.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你独立到不需要任何人。

paragraphs.en: It does not create a fixed identity based on interpersonal distance.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示存在固定的亲密距离身份。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean you regulate contact this way in every relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你在所有关系里都这样调节。

paragraphs.en: This interpretation concerns relative choices in these 24 questions. Responses can vary with the person, familiarity, current pressure and the seriousness of an event. A lower count does not mean being unable to love, immature or less capable.
paragraphs.zh: 这里只解释本次 24 题里你相对更常选择的方向。行为会随关系对象、熟悉程度、当下压力和事件严重程度变化；较低方向不表示不会爱、不成熟或能力不足。

headline.en: Repair Engagement received the most choices in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次题组中，参与分歧修复被选中的次数最多

summary.en: Clarifying impact, discussing another step and finding a way to resume cooperation received the most choices in this bank.
summary.zh: 看完你的回答，次数最多的方向是参与分歧修复——先澄清影响、先找下一步、先恢复合作的那类选项。

title.en: Repair Engagement: Love Personality Test Result
title.zh: 参与分歧修复：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Read Repair Engagement in the Love Personality Test: impact, possible next steps, willingness and boundaries, without grading relationship ability or outcomes.
description.zh: 完整阅读恋爱人格测试“参与分歧修复”：核对影响、提出可拒绝的小步骤与安全边界；次数不证明修复能力，也不预测关系结果。

scoreReading.en: The direction attached to a chosen option receives one count. Every direction appears in 12 comparisons. Repair Engagement is highest in this attempt. This is not a population percentile, accuracy rate or intensity, and it does not grade relationship competence.
scoreReading.zh: 计分方式：每次选中记 1 次，四个方向各参与 12 次比较。本次参与分歧修复次数最多。这个数字只在本次题组内部成立，不是人群百分位，不是准确率，更不是浓度。

paragraphs.en: Repair Engagement is FermatMind’s name for an entry after misunderstanding or disagreement: clarifying impact, taking the part that is yours, considering a small step either person may refuse, and checking whether continued discussion is safe. It does not establish maturity or skill at maintaining relationships. A counted choice cannot determine responsibility for harm.
paragraphs.zh: 参与分歧修复是费马测试自建的记忆符号，标记一种互动入口：误解或分歧后愿意澄清影响，承担自己能够承担的部分，提出双方可以拒绝的小步骤，并判断是否具备继续对话的安全条件。它不等同更会经营关系或更成熟。

title.zh: 本次题目中的具体观察

paragraphs.en: The relevant options look for how to continue a discussion, take part in dealing with a misunderstanding, discuss what to do after an impact, or find one workable point as a disagreement heats up. They describe selected entries into an interaction. They do not establish repair ability, another person’s willingness or the eventual effect.
paragraphs.zh: 分歧刚出现时，你倾向寻找之后可以怎样继续讨论；意识到彼此误解时，你愿意先参与处理当下的互动；自己的做法影响到对方时，你倾向先商量接下来可以怎样处理；争执升温时，题目观察的是先找一个可以继续处理的具体点。这是本次作答入口，不代表修复能力或关系效果。

paragraphs.en: When disagreement begins, you select looking for how the discussion could continue.
paragraphs.zh: 分歧刚出现时，选择寻找之后可以怎样继续讨论。

paragraphs.en: When misunderstanding becomes apparent, you select taking part in addressing the interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到彼此误解时，选择先参与处理当下的互动。

paragraphs.en: When your action affects someone, you select discussing what could be done next.
paragraphs.zh: 自己的做法影响到对方时，选择先商量接下来可以怎样处理。

paragraphs.en: When an argument heats up, you select finding one specific point that could still be addressed.
paragraphs.zh: 争执升温时，选择先找一个可以继续处理的具体点。

title.zh: 表达与回应的具体表现

paragraphs.en: Your selections more often favoured clarifying impact, discussing later handling or finding a small step. These responses do not establish greater maturity or a better relationship outcome. A proposal and its reception remain separate observations: the count cannot predict whether someone will want to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 本次题组显示，你较常选中澄清影响、商量后续处理或寻找小步骤的入口。这些选择不证明你更成熟或更会经营关系，也不能预测对方是否愿意继续。

paragraphs.en: A small disagreement and an event involving principles or safety may need different responses. This variation was not measured.
paragraphs.zh: 事件较轻或涉及原则、安全时，你可能采取不同入口；题目没有测量这个变化。

paragraphs.en: If the other person does or does not want to continue, you might negotiate, pause or end contact. Check the actual circumstances.
paragraphs.zh: 对方愿意或不愿意继续时，你会继续商量、暂停还是结束接触，请以实际经历判断。

paragraphs.en: Under your own pressure, you might want immediate handling or more time. The score cannot predict the order.
paragraphs.zh: 自己压力增加时，你可能更想立即处理，也可能需要等待；本次结果不预测顺序。

paragraphs.en: If the same issue returns, assess actual feedback rather than assume repeating a repair attempt will help.
paragraphs.zh: 同类问题重复出现时，这个入口是否仍常见，需要回看实际反馈。

title.en: When this entry may be useful

paragraphs.en: When it is safe and both people want to continue, one specific point can offer a possible restart. Assess its use through what follows.
paragraphs.zh: 在安全且双方愿意继续交流时，找一个具体处理点可作为重新开始的尝试；是否有用需看后续反馈。

paragraphs.en: Checking a particular impact can define the subject being discussed without deciding responsibility in advance.
paragraphs.zh: 核对具体影响可以帮助界定当下在讨论什么；不代表责任已经确定。

paragraphs.en: A small proposal is an observable entry into conversation, not a guarantee of acceptance, refusal or any response.
paragraphs.zh: 提出小步骤只是一个可观察的沟通入口，不保证对方接受、拒绝或回应。

paragraphs.en: Review what happened after discussing a next step. The original choice does not establish relationship quality or its future.
paragraphs.zh: 可以回看：商量后续处理之后，实际发生了什么？不从这个选择推导关系质量或结局。

paragraphs.en: Before proposing further handling, check whether the other person wants continued discussion now.
paragraphs.zh: 提出后续处理前，可以检查对方当下是否愿意继续，不预设此时继续就一定合适。

paragraphs.en: Revisit a repair attempt: were you addressing an impact you actually caused, or also assuming responsibility that belonged elsewhere?
paragraphs.zh: 回看一次修复尝试：你处理的是自己确实造成的影响，还是把其他责任也放进来了？

paragraphs.en: In unsafe or repeatedly unworkable situations, stopping is an option. This result never requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 对于不安全或反复无效的情境，停止修复也是可选项；本结果不要求继续接触。

paragraphs.en: For example, after an argument you ask whether the other person wants to discuss what happened and what could change.
paragraphs.zh: 一次争执后，你第二天主动说：昨天那件事，我想再聊聊怎么避免。

paragraphs.en: If you recognise that your words caused an impact, you acknowledge the specific impact and ask whether a proposed action would be welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 你意识到自己说重了话，先承认影响，再问对方希望你怎么弥补。

paragraphs.en: When both people are tired and willing, you might agree on a small ordinary activity and a later conversation. Neither sharing a meal nor restarting a discussion is obligatory.
paragraphs.zh: 双方都累了谈不下去，你提出先做一件小事（比如一起吃饭），再约时间谈正事。

paragraphs.en: Before a repair attempt, check safety and whether the other person actually wants to talk.
paragraphs.zh: 修复前先问一句：这件事的安全边界是什么？对方真的愿意谈吗？

paragraphs.en: Take responsibility only for what is yours rather than absorbing another person’s conduct into your task.
paragraphs.zh: 只承担自己确实造成的那部分，不替对方的问题买单。

paragraphs.en: If attempts are repeatedly refused, allow yourself to stop. A count never requires pursuing someone.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方反复拒绝修复，允许自己停下来，而不是继续追着修。

paragraphs.en: Have you included responsibility that was not yours in a repair attempt?
paragraphs.zh: 你有没有把不属于自己的责任也揽进修复里？

paragraphs.en: Were you mainly trying to keep the conversation going, or checking what the other person actually wanted?
paragraphs.zh: 修复时你更关注让对话继续，还是让对方真正好受？

paragraphs.en: In a situation involving violence, coercion or ongoing harm, did immediate safety take priority?
paragraphs.zh: 遇到暴力、胁迫或持续伤害时，你会优先保护自己的安全吗？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: It does not establish greater maturity or relationship skill.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更会经营关系或更成熟。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean you can save a relationship or that every relationship should continue.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你能挽救关系，也不表示所有关系都应该继续。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean every disagreement can be resolved through conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示分歧一定可以通过沟通解决。

paragraphs.en: It never makes repair a one-person responsibility.
paragraphs.zh: 不要求你单方面承担修复责任。

paragraphs.en: It does not seek shared causes or shared blame for violence, coercion, control or harm.
paragraphs.zh: 不为暴力、胁迫、控制或伤害寻找双向原因。

paragraphs.en: This interpretation concerns relative choices in these 24 questions. Responses can vary with the person, familiarity, current pressure and the seriousness of an event. A lower count does not mean being unable to love, immature or less capable.
paragraphs.zh: 这里只解释本次 24 题里你相对更常选择的方向。行为会随关系对象、熟悉程度、当下压力和事件严重程度变化；较低方向不表示不会爱、不成熟或能力不足。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration questionnaire has not completed reliability, validity or population-norm studies and has no official certification. Its self-reported choice counts are not an attachment assessment, relationship diagnosis or commercial relationship course.
paragraphs.zh: 本内容用于娱乐与自我探索，尚未完成信度、效度、常模等心理测量学验证，也未获得任何官方认证。结果仅基于本次自报选择的次数比较，不等同依恋类型诊断、关系诊断或任何商业恋爱课程。

headline.en: Clear Expression & Attuned Response have equal highest counts in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次选择中，清楚表达与留意回应的原始次数并列最高

summary.en: In these 24 choices, putting something into words and first listening were selected equally often, jointly above the other entries.
summary.zh: 这次题组里，说清楚和先听这两个方向被选中的次数一样多，且都排在最高位。

title.en: Expression & Response Tie: Love Personality Result
title.zh: 表达与回应并列：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Explore an Expression–Response tie: equal highest choice counts, speaking and listening examples, checking feedback and why the tie sets no fixed sequence.
description.zh: 理解表达与回应原始次数并列最高：比较说清楚与先倾听的具体情境、信息核对与取舍，不把并列解释成固定组合或自动顺序。

scoreReading.en: Each selected option adds one count to its direction. These two directions have equal counts, both above the other two. The result retains both leaders; question order, codes and option position never choose a winner. Equal counts do not establish a permanent combination or how these responses work together.
scoreReading.zh: 每道题只给被选中的方向记 1 次；本次清楚表达和留意回应的次数相同，并且都高于另外两个方向。系统完整保留并列，不用题号、代码或选项位置分出先后——两个方向同时居首，就是本次的真实结果。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression: Clear Expression counts selections that state feelings, needs, boundaries or arrangements. Here its count equals Attuned Response.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达：你的清楚表达次数，来自把感受、需要、边界或安排直接说清楚的题目；这一次它和留意回应并列居首。

paragraphs.en: Attuned Response: Attuned Response counts first listening, checking a meaning or considering willingness to engage. Here its count equals Clear Expression.
paragraphs.zh: 留意回应：你的留意回应次数，来自先听、先核对、先看对方当下状态的题目；这一次它和清楚表达拿到的次数一样多。

paragraphs.en: Recall wanting to explain something while also noticing someone’s state. Which action actually came first, and what information guided it?
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次你想表达某件事，同时又在观察对方状态的时刻，最后哪一边占了上风？

paragraphs.en: Compare a very familiar person with someone you have recently met. Did the space taken by speaking and listening change?
paragraphs.zh: 和特别熟的人、刚认识的人分别相处时，你说的和听的比例是否不同？

paragraphs.en: When someone was visibly upset, did you open your topic, ask permission or wait? The score does not supply that detail.
paragraphs.zh: 对方情绪明显不好时，你是先开口还是先等？

paragraphs.en: When a decision affects both people, do you first describe its meaning for you or ask for their view?
paragraphs.zh: 遇到影响彼此的事，你更常先说明自己的意思，还是先问对方怎么想？

paragraphs.en: Which subjects seem to call for a direct statement, and which have led you to check the moment first?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些话题适合直接说，哪些话题你其实会先看时机？

paragraphs.en: In a specific conversation, where did explaining your side and checking theirs appear in the sequence?
paragraphs.zh: 对话里，你说清楚的部分和核对对方的部分，通常哪个更靠前？

paragraphs.en: Can you recall finishing an explanation before discovering that the other person had not been listening?
paragraphs.zh: 你有没有过把话都说完了，才发现对方根本没在听的情况？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: This tie cannot identify which of these directions appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. The questionnaire did not measure that sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下清楚表达或留意回应哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: Under pressure, did you first speak or listen? Use a specific episode rather than this tied result.
paragraphs.zh: 压力出现时，你实际先做的是说话还是倾听？

paragraphs.en: What were your roles, time constraints and the other person’s observable circumstances?
paragraphs.zh: 当时的角色、时间限制和对方状态分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, what did that choice make room for, and what did it leave out?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那个选择帮助了什么，又漏掉了什么？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: When the atmosphere stiffens, do you try to explain the issue or first check willingness to talk?
paragraphs.zh: 气氛变僵时，你是倾向把话说开，还是先确认对方愿不愿意谈？

paragraphs.en: If someone remains quiet, what did you actually do: ask again, wait, or end the discussion?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方一直沉默，你更常追问，还是更常等？

paragraphs.en: Take a recent important conversation and mark the sentences in which you explained something and the places where you checked understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 找最近一次重要对话，标出你开口说清楚和停下来核对的句子。

paragraphs.en: Recall a moment when someone seemed about to speak and stopped. Separate what you observed from what you assumed.
paragraphs.zh: 回看一次对方欲言又止的场景，你当时做了什么。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: Before a direct explanation, consider asking, “Do you have room to hear something now?”
paragraphs.zh: 下次想直接说清楚前，先问一句：对方现在有余量听吗？

paragraphs.en: After listening and checking, include your own need if you want it heard.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想先听时，说完核对的话之后，补上你自己的需要。

paragraphs.en: Compare one conversation with more speaking and one with more listening. Ask which fitted its circumstances rather than declare either universally better.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次说多听少和一次听多说少的对话，哪种更适合当时。

paragraphs.en: Which offered choices in this bank led you toward explaining, and which toward listening?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，说清楚和先听的题目各把你带向哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: Would the situation change with someone you fully trust? Treat this as a question, not a predicted switch.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方是你完全信任的人，你的比例会变吗？

paragraphs.en: Compare an explanation that was not received as expected with an episode in which listening first seemed useful.
paragraphs.zh: 回想一次你话说完但对方没接住，和一次你先听反而谈拢的经历。

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: Two co-leading counts are not a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这两种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: They do not prove that you are both articulate and considerate or a more complete partner.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你既会表达又体贴，是更全面的伴侣。

paragraphs.en: They cannot guarantee another person understands you.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你能保证对方更理解你。

paragraphs.en: They reveal no other person’s feelings or judgment of you.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: They predict neither compatibility nor how long a relationship will last.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: The tie records equal highest counts in this attempt. How speaking and listening combine, or when you choose one, needs actual examples; the test does not decide it.
paragraphs.zh: 并列只记录本次 24 题里两个方向原始次数相同；至于两种方式如何配合、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

headline.en: Clear Expression & Space Regulation have equal highest counts in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次选择中，清楚表达与调节靠近与空间的原始次数并列最高

summary.en: Stating something clearly and first making space received equal highest counts across these 24 choices.
summary.zh: 这次题组里，把话说明白和先留出空间这两个方向被选中的次数相同，且都排在最高位。

title.en: Expression & Space Tie: Love Personality Result
title.zh: 表达与空间并列：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Explore an Expression–Space tie: direct words, timing, possible pauses and return arrangements. Equal highest counts do not decide when to speak or step back.
description.zh: 理解表达与空间原始次数并列最高：比较直说、选择时机、暂停与重新联系的例子；并列不替你决定何时靠近或退开。

scoreReading.en: Each selected option adds one count to its direction. These two directions have equal counts, both above the other two. The result retains both leaders; question order, codes and option position never choose a winner. Equal counts do not establish a permanent combination or how these responses work together.
scoreReading.zh: 计分时每道题选中谁，谁就记 1 次；本次清楚表达和调节靠近与空间的次数打平，且都高于其余方向。并列原样保留，不使用题号、字母顺序或选项位置破同分。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression: Clear Expression counts selections such as explaining sooner and stating an arrangement. Its count equals Space Regulation here.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达：你的清楚表达次数，来自尽早说、说明白、把安排讲清楚的题目；这一次它和调节空间次数相同。

paragraphs.en: Space Regulation: Space Regulation counts leaving room, adjusting contact intensity and pausing a conversation. Its count equals Clear Expression here.
paragraphs.zh: 调节靠近与空间：你的调节空间次数，来自先留出空间、调整联系强度、暂停当前对话的题目；这一次它和清楚表达打了平手。

paragraphs.en: Recall wanting to speak soon while also wanting a suitable moment. What did you ultimately do, and why at that time?
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次你想尽早说，同时又想等一个合适时机的时刻，最后怎么处理的？

paragraphs.en: Compare needing solitude with needing to express a request. Did your priorities differ?
paragraphs.zh: 需要独处和需要表达需求时，你的优先顺序是否不同？

paragraphs.en: When someone was busy or tired, did you continue, ask about timing or leave the subject for later?
paragraphs.zh: 对方正忙或正累时，你是照说，还是先看时间点？

paragraphs.en: For an important topic, do your examples show immediate explanation or waiting until both people have capacity?
paragraphs.zh: 重要的话，你更常马上说，还是更常选双方都从容的时机？

paragraphs.en: Which information needed to be timely, and which could safely wait?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些内容必须及时说，哪些可以等一等？

paragraphs.en: When expressing a need for space, did you state it directly or only change your availability?
paragraphs.zh: 你表达的时候，是先把话说完，还是先说明自己需要一点空间？

paragraphs.en: Have you held something back and later discovered the other person did not know there was an issue?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你憋着没说，后来发现对方根本不知道发生了什么？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: This tie cannot identify which of these directions appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. The questionnaire did not measure that sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下清楚表达或调节空间哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: In the particular pressured moment, did you first speak or step away?
paragraphs.zh: 压力出现时，你先说还是先退开？

paragraphs.en: What was observable about the other person’s state, and what did you know about your own?
paragraphs.zh: 当时对方的状态和你自己的状态分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Afterward, did that action clarify the situation, increase uncertainty or have another effect?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那个选择让事情更清楚，还是更远了？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: When an atmosphere changes, did you explain what was wrong or first step back?
paragraphs.zh: 气氛不对时，你更常把话摊开，还是更常先各退一步？

paragraphs.en: Before a pause, did you describe whether and how you intended to return?
paragraphs.zh: 暂停之前，你会把回来的安排说清楚吗？

paragraphs.en: Examine an occasion when you waited and talked later. Was the pause wanted, and what information did it give each person?
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你选择先不说、后来再谈的经历，核对当时真的需要空间吗。

paragraphs.en: Examine an occasion when a direct explanation surprised someone. Check timing without assuming it was the only cause.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你直接说了、对方措手不及的经历，核对时机是不是问题。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: Before speaking, check available capacity; before stepping back, describe a possible return arrangement if safe and wanted.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想说前，先确认对方当前的余量；下次想退开前，把回来的时间一起说。

paragraphs.en: In an ordinary moment when you do not need distance, consider saying what your plans are.
paragraphs.zh: 试着在不需要空间时主动说一次自己的安排。

paragraphs.en: Compare a useful direct statement and a useful pause. Write what differed about their circumstances rather than nominate a winning style.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次直说成功和一次留空间成功的场景，比较它们分别赢在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Which paired choices drew you toward explaining and which toward space?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，直说和留空间的题目分别对应你的哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: If the other person seemed well rested, would you want to speak sooner? A tie does not answer that hypothetical.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方最近状态很好，你会不会更愿意直说？

paragraphs.en: The last time you needed solitude, did you explain your reason and any intended next contact?
paragraphs.zh: 你上一次需要独处时，有没有把原因告诉对方？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: This does not create a fixed combination or love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这两种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: Wanting space does not establish avoidance, fear of intimacy or insufficient love.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你需要空间就是回避、害怕亲密或不够爱。

paragraphs.en: The tie does not prove ideal honesty and good judgment about distance.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你既坦诚又有分寸，是更理想的伴侣。

paragraphs.en: It does not reveal another person’s feelings or opinion.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: It does not predict compatibility or relationship duration.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: This result records equal highest counts, not a rule for choosing between direct speech and space. Compare actual timing, wishes and feedback to understand the tradeoff.
paragraphs.zh: 并列只记录本次 24 题里两个方向原始次数相同；至于直说和留空间如何取舍、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

headline.zh: 本次选择中，清楚表达与参与分歧修复的原始次数并列最高

summary.en: Explaining a view and looking for a way to address a disagreement received equal highest counts in this attempt.
summary.zh: 这次题组里，把话说完整和把分歧接回去这两个方向被选中的次数一样多，且都排在最高位。

title.en: Expression & Repair Tie: Love Personality Result
title.zh: 表达与修复并列：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Explore an Expression–Repair tie: clarifying meaning, checking impact and offering a next step. Equal counts do not require a relationship to continue.
description.zh: 理解表达与修复原始次数并列最高：比较澄清意思、核对影响与后续步骤；不评价成熟度，不要求任何关系继续。

scoreReading.en: Each selected option adds one count to its direction. These two directions have equal counts, both above the other two. The result retains both leaders; question order, codes and option position never choose a winner. Equal counts do not establish a permanent combination or how these responses work together.
scoreReading.zh: 每道题选中哪个方向，哪个方向就记 1 次；本次清楚表达和参与分歧修复的数量相等，且都高于另外两个方向。并列完整保留，不用题号、代码或选项位置去分先后。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression: Clear Expression counts explaining a view fully, restating intended meaning and asking a clear question. It ties with Repair Engagement here.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达：你的清楚表达次数，来自把看法说完整、重新说明原意、提出清楚问题的题目；这一次它和参与修复并列居首。

paragraphs.en: Repair Engagement: Repair Engagement counts finding a next step, agreeing on continued handling or considering amends. It ties with Clear Expression here.
paragraphs.zh: 参与分歧修复：你的参与修复次数，来自寻找下一步、约定继续处理的步骤、一起确认弥补方式的题目；这一次它和清楚表达拿到的次数一样多。

paragraphs.en: In a recent disagreement, did you explain your position or look for how to continue the discussion? Identify what actually happened.
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次分歧里，你更常把立场讲完，还是更常找下一步怎么谈？

paragraphs.en: After a misunderstanding, did you first clarify meaning or address the interaction around it?
paragraphs.zh: 误解发生后，你先澄清原意，还是先修复气氛？

paragraphs.en: After an argument ended, did you explain further, arrange a later review or choose neither?
paragraphs.zh: 争执结束后，你是把话说透，还是主动约下一次复盘？

paragraphs.en: When disagreement first appeared, did you finish your view or look for a path to another discussion?
paragraphs.zh: 分歧刚出现时，你更常把看法说完，还是更常先找继续谈的路径？

paragraphs.en: Which disagreements seemed suitable for immediate clarification, and which needed an agreed later time?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些分歧适合当场说清，哪些适合先约定时间再谈？

paragraphs.en: While you explained your meaning, what explicit feedback showed what the other person heard?
paragraphs.zh: 你解释自己的意思时，对方是在听内容，还是在看你的态度？

paragraphs.en: Can you recall a carefully reasoned explanation after which the interaction became harder? Do not presume the explanation was the only cause.
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你把道理说得很清楚，但关系反而更僵了？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: This tie cannot identify which of these directions appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. The questionnaire did not measure that sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下清楚表达或参与修复哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: In a pressured disagreement, did you first explain or look for a repair point?
paragraphs.zh: 压力下的分歧里，你实际先做的是说清楚还是找修复点？

paragraphs.en: How serious was the event, and what did each person say about their capacity?
paragraphs.zh: 当时的事件严重程度和双方状态分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, was missing information, the interaction process or something else the main obstacle?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那次对话缺的是内容还是过程？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: Before discussing amends, did you establish the particular impact or jump to a proposed solution?
paragraphs.zh: 修复的时候，你是先确认影响，还是先给出弥补方案？

paragraphs.en: If the other person did not want to talk, did you respect that choice or keep pursuing discussion?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方不想谈，你还会继续追着修吗？

paragraphs.en: Review an explanation after which someone became more upset. Check what happened in the process rather than diagnose their reaction.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你解释得很清楚但对方更生气的情景，核对是不是过程出了问题。

paragraphs.en: Review a rushed repair attempt. Was the other person’s account heard before a next step was offered?
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你急着修复、跳过对方情绪的情景，核对效果如何。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: After your explanation, leave room for the other person to say what did not make sense to them.
paragraphs.zh: 下次分歧里，先说完自己的部分，再问对方哪里没接住。

paragraphs.en: Before arranging a review, check that the other person wants one.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想约复盘前，先确认对方真的愿意谈。

paragraphs.en: Compare a disagreement that needed clarification with one that needed a different process. Keep safety and responsibility separate from a wish to resume contact.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次说清更重要和一次修复更重要的分歧。

paragraphs.en: Which choices led you toward explaining, and which toward a next step?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，说清楚和找下一步的题目分别把你带向哪里？

paragraphs.en: If a disagreement involves a principle or safety, would continuing a repair attempt be appropriate?
paragraphs.zh: 如果分歧涉及原则或安全，你还会急着修复吗？

paragraphs.en: Have you apologised for a responsibility that was not yours?
paragraphs.zh: 你有没有为不属于自己的责任道过歉？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: The tie is not a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这两种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: It does not establish greater maturity or relationship-management skill.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更会经营关系或更成熟。

paragraphs.en: It does not mean every disagreement is solvable through discussion or every relationship must be repaired.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示所有分歧都能靠沟通解决，也不表示关系必须修复。

paragraphs.en: It does not reveal another person’s feelings or opinion.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: It predicts neither partner fit nor how long a relationship will last.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: This tie records two equal highest counts. How clarification and repair are combined or sequenced must be checked against actual experiences; continuing contact is never required by the result.
paragraphs.zh: 并列只记录本次 24 题里两个方向原始次数相同；至于说清和修复如何搭配、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

title.en: Response & Space Tie: Love Personality Result

description.en: Explore a Response–Space tie: asking, silence and room to think, with concrete checks. Equal counts cannot tell you what another person wants.
description.zh: 理解回应与空间原始次数并列最高：比较询问、沉默与整理时间的具体例子；次数不替对方表达意愿，也不说明你更体贴。

scoreReading.en: Each selected option adds one count to its direction. These two directions have equal counts, both above the other two. The result retains both leaders; question order, codes and option position never choose a winner. Equal counts do not establish a permanent combination or how these responses work together.
scoreReading.zh: 每道题只给被选中的方向加 1 次；本次留意回应和调节靠近与空间的次数打平，且都高于另外两个方向。系统保留全部并列，不借助题号、代码或选项位置做任何区分。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Attuned Response: Attuned Response counts asking whether someone wants to talk, checking a response and asking about silence. Its count equals Space Regulation here.
paragraphs.zh: 留意回应：你的留意回应次数，来自询问是否想说、跟随对方回应方式、确认沉默含义的题目；这一次它和调节空间并列居首。

paragraphs.en: Space Regulation: Space Regulation counts room to gather thoughts, a slower conversation and keeping distance. Its count equals Attuned Response here.
paragraphs.zh: 调节靠近与空间：你的调节空间次数，来自给对方整理空间、放慢交流节奏并留出停顿、保留距离的题目；这一次它和留意回应拿到的次数一样多。

paragraphs.en: When someone’s mood changed, did you ask about it or first leave room? Describe the action without claiming to know their feelings.
paragraphs.zh: 对方情绪有变化时，你更常问，还是更常先给空间？

paragraphs.en: When someone stayed quiet, did you check what was wanted or wait for another signal?
paragraphs.zh: 对方沉默时，你是去确认这份沉默，还是先等新信号？

paragraphs.en: When preferred contact frequencies differed, did you first understand the signal or negotiate a range?
paragraphs.zh: 联系频率不一致时，你先理解对方信号，还是先协商范围？

paragraphs.en: When information was unclear, did you ask or hold back? What did you know at the time?
paragraphs.zh: 对方的信号不明朗时，你更常开口问，还是更常按兵不动？

paragraphs.en: Which examples suggest that a question fitted the moment, and which suggest that space was wanted?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些时候主动问更好，哪些时候给空间更好？

paragraphs.en: When checking someone’s state, what explicit feedback showed how the question was received?
paragraphs.zh: 你核对对方状态时，对方能感觉到你在问，还是觉得你在试探？

paragraphs.en: Have you left space when the other person later said they had wanted you to speak?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你留了空间，对方却希望你先开口？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: This tie cannot identify which of these directions appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. The questionnaire did not measure that sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下留意回应或调节空间哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: Under pressure, did you move closer to ask or first step back?
paragraphs.zh: 压力出现时，你更常凑近问，还是更常退一步？

paragraphs.en: What did the other person actually request, and how did that compare with your assumption?
paragraphs.zh: 当时对方需要的和你以为对方需要的，是否一致？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, which parts of the decision came from information and which from guessing?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，你的判断有多少来自信号，多少来自猜测？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: If someone wanted company, was that what you offered, or did you assume distance was preferable?
paragraphs.zh: 对方需要陪伴时，你给的是陪伴还是空间？

paragraphs.en: After a pause, did you choose to reconnect, leave an arrangement or do something else?
paragraphs.zh: 暂停之后，你会主动重新联系吗？

paragraphs.en: Review a quiet moment when you waited: did a new signal arrive, and what did it actually establish?
paragraphs.zh: 找一次对方沉默你选择了等待的经历，核对后来信号是否真的来了。

paragraphs.en: Review a direct question after which someone explicitly said they felt more at ease. Compare the circumstances rather than make a universal rule.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你主动询问后对方反而轻松的经历，比较两种做法的差异。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: When unsure and safe to ask, consider, “Would you prefer company or some space?”
paragraphs.zh: 下次不确定时，直接问一句：你现在需要陪伴还是空间？

paragraphs.en: Before leaving room, describe a possible reconnection arrangement if you want one.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想给空间前，把重新联系的安排一起说出来。

paragraphs.en: Compare a well-received question with a pause someone said they wanted. Their clear feedback is more informative than the tied count.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次问对了和一次退对了的场景。

paragraphs.en: Which choices prompted asking, and which prompted giving space?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，询问和给空间的题目分别对应你的哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: What tends to happen when you also state your own need?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你先说出自己的需要，对方通常怎么回应？

paragraphs.en: Have you interpreted silence as rejection before obtaining enough information?
paragraphs.zh: 你有没有把对方的沉默误读成拒绝？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: This does not establish a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这两种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: A wish for space does not establish avoidance, coldness or fear of intimacy.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你需要空间就是回避、冷漠或害怕亲密。

paragraphs.en: The count does not establish greater kindness, consideration or empathy.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更体贴、更善良或有更强的同理心。

paragraphs.en: It does not reveal another person’s feelings or judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: It does not predict relationship fit or duration.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: Equal counts do not settle the choice between a question and space. Examine actual requests, timing and information, without treating a guess about silence as a fact.
paragraphs.zh: 并列只记录本次 24 题里两个方向原始次数相同；至于询问和留空间如何取舍、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

summary.zh: 这次题组里，先理解对方和先推进修复这两个方向被选中的次数一样多，且都排在最高位。

title.en: Response & Repair Tie: Love Personality Result

paragraphs.en: Repair Engagement: Repair Engagement counts another attempt, considering amends and arranging a review. It ties with Attuned Response here.
paragraphs.zh: 参与分歧修复：你的参与修复次数，来自推动找到下一次尝试、确认如何弥补、主动安排复盘的题目；这一次它和留意回应拿到的次数一样多。

paragraphs.en: When discussion stalled, did you check an unheard point or encourage another attempt?
paragraphs.zh: 讨论不顺时，你更常找没被听见的话，还是更常推动下一次尝试？

paragraphs.en: When someone described an impact, did you first hear the specific feeling or discuss possible amends?
paragraphs.zh: 对方指出受影响时，你先理解感受，还是先确认弥补？

paragraphs.en: After an argument, did you ask about anything left unsaid or propose a later review?
paragraphs.zh: 争执结束后，你先问对方还有什么补充，还是先约复盘？

paragraphs.en: When someone was still upset, did you listen first or suggest a next step? Check their stated wishes rather than infer that one was better.
paragraphs.zh: 对方还没消气时，你更常先听，还是更常先约下一步？

paragraphs.en: In which experience did listening itself form part of addressing a misunderstanding?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些时候倾听本身就是在修复？

paragraphs.en: After checking a feeling, was there an opening to continue if both people wanted it?
paragraphs.zh: 你核对对方感受之后，有没有留下可以继续谈的入口？

paragraphs.en: Have you kept asking questions without clarifying what would happen next, and what feedback did you receive?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你只问不推进，对方反而觉得你在绕？

paragraphs.en: During a pressured disagreement, did understanding or a proposed repair come first?
paragraphs.zh: 压力下的分歧里，你实际先做的是理解还是修复？

paragraphs.en: What did the other person actually say, and what kind of event was being discussed?
paragraphs.zh: 当时对方的状态和事件的性质分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Afterward, did the situation appear to need listening, action or something outside those two options?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那次最缺的是倾听还是行动？

paragraphs.en: Before a repair attempt, did you confirm willingness to talk?
paragraphs.zh: 修复之前，你确认过对方真的愿意谈吗？

paragraphs.en: If attempts were repeatedly refused, did you stop or continue proposing them? A result cannot require pursuit.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方反复拒绝修复，你还会继续推进吗？

paragraphs.en: Review an episode in which listening before a later discussion was explicitly welcomed.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你先安抚情绪、再谈正事反而顺利的经历。

paragraphs.en: Review an attempt to resolve something quickly that skipped the other person’s account. Separate the observed outcome from assumptions about why it happened.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你急着修复、跳过倾听而失败的对话。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: Before offering a repair step, allow the other person to finish if they want to speak.
paragraphs.zh: 下次修复前，先完整听完对方，再提步骤。

paragraphs.en: After listening, ask whether anything should happen next instead of assuming discussion needs an action.
paragraphs.zh: 下次只倾听不动时，补一句：那我们接下来可以怎么处理？

paragraphs.en: Compare an occasion where listening was enough for the stated request with one where a concrete agreed action was wanted.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次倾听足够和一次需要行动的场景。

paragraphs.en: Which questions led you toward understanding and which toward another step?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，理解和推进的题目分别把你带向哪里？

paragraphs.en: Have you assumed listening alone completed what the other person was asking for?
paragraphs.zh: 你有没有把倾听当成修复的全部？

paragraphs.en: If listening without advice is requested, are you willing to leave it there?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方需要的只是倾听，你会满足于不给建议吗？

scoreReading.zh: 每道题只给被选中的方向记 1 次；本次调节靠近与空间和参与分歧修复的次数打平，且都高于另外两个方向。并列会原样保留，不因题号顺序、字母顺序或选项位置而分先后。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Space Regulation: Space Regulation counts pausing a conversation, lowering interaction intensity and protecting time to gather thoughts. It ties with Repair Engagement here.
paragraphs.zh: 调节靠近与空间：你的调节空间次数，来自先暂停当前对话、先降低互动强度、保护整理时间的题目；这一次它和参与修复并列居首。

paragraphs.en: Repair Engagement: Repair Engagement counts a specific workable point, a small repair action and a possible return to discussion. It ties with Space Regulation here.
paragraphs.zh: 参与分歧修复：你的参与修复次数，来自先找一个可以继续处理的具体点、先完成小的修复动作、确认重新接上对话的题目；这一次它和调节空间拿到的次数一样多。

paragraphs.en: As an argument heated up, did you propose a pause or continue looking for one point to address?
paragraphs.zh: 争执升温时，你更常提议暂停，还是更常继续找修复点？

paragraphs.en: When both people were tired, did you lower intensity or propose a small action?
paragraphs.zh: 双方都很疲惫时，你先降强度，还是先做一个小动作？

paragraphs.en: When contact felt strained, did you renegotiate space or how a disagreement would be handled?
paragraphs.zh: 关系出现拉扯时，你先重新商量空间，还是先重新商量分歧？

paragraphs.en: Before emotions had settled, did you stop the discussion or continue despite the strain?
paragraphs.zh: 情绪还没降下来时，你更常暂停，还是更常硬着头皮谈？

paragraphs.en: Which issues needed time before discussion, and which seemed workable then? Safety can rule out continued contact entirely.
paragraphs.zh: 哪些分歧必须停下来再谈，哪些可以当场处理？

paragraphs.en: When proposing a pause, did you also describe a possible return arrangement?
paragraphs.zh: 你提议暂停时，会把回来的安排一起说清楚吗？

paragraphs.en: Has someone interpreted a pause differently from how you intended it? Use their actual statement rather than infer a motive.
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你暂停了，对方却觉得你在逃避？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: This tie cannot identify which of these directions appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. The questionnaire did not measure that sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下调节空间或参与修复哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: As conflict rose, did you step back or move toward another step?
paragraphs.zh: 冲突升温时，你实际先做的是退一步还是进一步？

paragraphs.en: How tired were both people, and how important or unsafe was the topic?
paragraphs.zh: 当时双方的疲惫程度和话题的重要性分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, was space, a concrete action or something else missing?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那次缺的是空间还是行动？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: In a particular episode, which actually came first: the pause or a repair proposal?
paragraphs.zh: 暂停和修复之间，你更常让哪一个先发生？

paragraphs.en: If the other person wanted neither, how did you respect that choice while keeping your own boundaries?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方不想暂停也不想修复，你会怎么办？

paragraphs.en: Review a pause after which both people were willing to return. What changed before the later conversation?
paragraphs.zh: 找一次暂停后双方都冷静、后来谈拢的经历。

paragraphs.en: Compare an occasion when pressing to continue made the discussion harder. Do not generalise from one episode to every conflict.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你坚持当场谈、结果越谈越僵的经历，比较暂停的价值。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: If you want a pause, describe a possible time to return without demanding agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 下次暂停时，把回来的时间一起约定。

paragraphs.en: If you want immediate repair, first ask whether continuing now is wanted and safe.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想立刻修复时，先问一句：现在都冷静了吗？

paragraphs.en: Compare a useful pause and a useful same-day discussion. Notice the conditions that differed instead of treating the tie as an automatic switch.
paragraphs.zh: 记录一次暂停更对和一次当场谈更对的场景。

paragraphs.en: Which choices drew you toward pausing, and which toward repair?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，暂停和修复的题目分别对应你的哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: In a particular pause, did you need time, wish to avoid a hard subject or have another reason?
paragraphs.zh: 你提议暂停时，是真的需要时间，还是在避开难谈的话？

paragraphs.en: If someone wants to talk immediately, what would let you acknowledge that request while keeping your own right to stop?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方需要的是当场谈，你能接受吗？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: This tie does not create a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这两种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: Needing space does not establish avoidance, coldness or fear of intimacy.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你需要空间就是回避、冷漠或害怕亲密。

paragraphs.en: The count does not establish maturity or repair skill, and it does not mean every disagreement can be repaired.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更会经营关系或更成熟，也不表示所有分歧都能修复。

paragraphs.en: It does not reveal another person’s feelings or opinion.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: It predicts neither compatibility nor relationship duration.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: This tie records equal highest counts for pause-related and repair-related choices. It does not dictate an order, guarantee resolution or require either person to keep talking.
paragraphs.zh: 并列只记录本次 24 题里两个方向原始次数相同；至于暂停和修复如何取舍、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

title.en: Clear Expression / Attuned Response / Space Regulation — Tied

headline.en: Three directions share the highest count in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次选择中，清楚表达、留意回应与调节靠近与空间的原始次数并列最高

summary.en: Putting something into words, listening first and leaving space received equal highest counts. The attempt supplies no unique leading entry.
summary.zh: 这次题组里，说清楚、先听、留空间三个方向被选中的次数相同，本次没有形成唯一的顶部方向。

title.en: Expression, Response & Space: Love Personality Tie
title.zh: 表达、回应与空间并列：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Read the Expression–Response–Space tie: three equal highest counts, conversation examples and ways to examine timing without inventing a combined personality.
description.zh: 理解表达、回应与空间三方向并列：完整计数读法、具体对话与时机核对；不推导混合人格、压力切换或关系适配。

scoreReading.en: These three directions have exactly equal counts, above the remaining direction in this 24-question attempt. All co-leaders are retained without using question order, codes or option position as a tiebreaker. The result establishes no complex personality, multiple identity or automatic way of combining the responses.
scoreReading.zh: 本次 24 题里，清楚表达、留意回应、调节靠近与空间被选中的次数完全相同，且都高于参与分歧修复。系统对并列不做任何处理，不靠题号、字母顺序或选项位置来分出先后。这不是多重人格或复杂人格，只是这次题组没有出现唯一领先的方向。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression: Counts come from selecting statements that put observations, feelings, needs, views or arrangements into words. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达：你的清楚表达次数，来自把观察、感受、需要或安排直接说清楚的题目；三个方向并列时，它和另外两个次数相同。

paragraphs.en: Attuned Response: Counts come from selecting listening, checking a meaning, asking about willingness or noticing what remains unheard. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 留意回应：你的留意回应次数，来自先听、先核对、先看对方当下状态的题目；它在这组并列里与其余两个方向一样多。

paragraphs.en: Space Regulation: Counts come from selecting adjusted contact, a slower pace, room to gather thoughts or a pause. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 调节靠近与空间：你的调节空间次数，来自调整联系强度、留出空间、暂停当前对话的题目；它在这组并列里与其余两个方向打了平手。

paragraphs.en: Recall an important conversation. Where did speaking, listening and leaving room actually appear? Mark the actions separately rather than assume they formed a helpful sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次重要对话里，你开口说、停下来听、和先缓一缓的时刻分别出现在哪里？

paragraphs.en: Compare a calm moment and a moment when someone was unsettled. Was the mix different, and what explicit feedback did you have?
paragraphs.zh: 对方情绪平稳和情绪起伏时，你的三种做法比例是否不同？

paragraphs.en: After time alone, did you explain your state or ask about theirs first? The tie does not tell you which.
paragraphs.zh: 独处一天后回来，你先说还是先听？

paragraphs.en: When something affects both people, do examples show you first explaining, asking or waiting?
paragraphs.zh: 遇到影响彼此的事，你更常先说明、先询问，还是先等？

paragraphs.en: Which subjects were suitable for immediate conversation, and which needed more capacity from both people?
paragraphs.zh: 哪些事情适合直接谈，哪些适合等双方都从容再说？

paragraphs.en: What actual sequence did explanation, checking and pausing follow in one conversation?
paragraphs.zh: 你的表达、核对和暂停，通常按什么顺序出现？

paragraphs.en: Have you used all three in a conversation that both people later described as useful? Do not assume the three-count tie proves that occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你三种都用上了，对话反而顺畅了？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: The equal counts cannot identify which direction appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. This bank did not measure a sequence or predict your reaction to stress.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下这三个方向哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: In the pressured moment, did you first speak, listen or step away?
paragraphs.zh: 压力出现时，你实际先做的是说、听还是退？

paragraphs.en: What roles, time pressure and observable circumstances affected that moment?
paragraphs.zh: 当时的角色、时间压力和对方状态分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, what did the first action make possible and what did it leave out?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，哪种先手帮了忙，哪种添了乱？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: When the atmosphere stiffened, did you explain the issue, ask whether discussion was wanted or step back?
paragraphs.zh: 气氛变僵时，你更常把话说开、先问意愿，还是先退一步？

paragraphs.en: If you made space, what information did the other person have about why and about any intended return?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你先让出空间，对方会不会反过来担心你生气了？

paragraphs.en: Take a recent conversation and separately mark your spoken explanation, your listening or checking, and any room you left.
paragraphs.zh: 找最近一次对话，分别标出你说、你听、你留空间的句子。

paragraphs.en: Review a pause followed by a later discussion. What changed during the pause, and was returning wanted by both people?
paragraphs.zh: 回看一次你先退开、后来谈成的经历，核对暂停的作用。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: Before opening a topic, consider asking about capacity. Before taking space, describe a possible return if safe and wanted.
paragraphs.zh: 下次开口前，先问：对方现在有余量吗？下次退开前，把回来的安排说好。

paragraphs.en: In an ordinary, mutually wanted conversation, notice opportunities for speaking, listening and pausing. You do not need to perform all three.
paragraphs.zh: 试着在一次对话里，把说、听、留空间各用一次。

paragraphs.en: If you want a private note, record the order that actually occurred and the feedback you received. One experience is not evidence of a permanent best sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 结束当天记一笔：今天哪种顺序让对话更顺。

paragraphs.en: Which questions led you toward speaking, listening and space?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，说、听、留空间三组题目各把你带向哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: Would being with someone you fully trust change what you want to do? This is for reflection, not a prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方是你最信任的人，你的比例会变吗？

paragraphs.en: Recall a conversation in which several approaches were used. What happened at each point, beyond the label you might give it?
paragraphs.zh: 回想一次三管齐下反而顺利的对话，当时是怎么做到的？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: Three co-leading counts do not form a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这三种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: They do not establish an ideally honest, considerate and well-balanced partner.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你既坦诚又体贴又有分寸，是更全面的伴侣。

paragraphs.en: They cannot guarantee another person feels understood or at ease.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你能保证对方更理解你或更自在。

paragraphs.en: They reveal no other person’s feelings or opinion of you.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: They predict neither compatibility nor relationship duration.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.en: Three equal highest counts mean there is no unique leader in this attempt. How speaking, listening and space appear in practice requires experiences, not an inferred switching pattern. A lower Repair Engagement count is not a deficit or a judgment about love.
paragraphs.zh: 三方向并列只说明本次题组没有形成唯一顶部方向；三种方式如何轮流出现、何时切换，需要你回到具体经历核对，测试不替你下结论。

paragraphs.en: This original self-exploration bank has not completed psychometric validation. It does not assign blame for harm. Safety takes priority over repair, and no result requires continued contact.
paragraphs.zh: 本原创题本尚未完成心理测量学验证，也不判断伤害中的责任归属。现实安全优先于修复，任何结果都不要求你继续接触。

title.en: Clear Expression / Attuned Response / Repair Engagement — Tied

headline.en: Three directions share the highest count in this attempt
headline.zh: 本次选择中，清楚表达、留意回应与参与分歧修复的原始次数并列最高

summary.en: Explaining, listening and looking for another step received equal highest counts, with no single leading direction in this attempt.
summary.zh: 这次题组里，说清楚、先听、找下一步三个方向被选中的次数相同，本次没有形成唯一的顶部方向。

title.en: Expression, Response & Repair: Love Personality Tie
title.zh: 表达、回应与修复并列：恋爱人格测试完整说明

description.en: Read the Expression–Response–Repair tie: three equal highest counts, hearing both accounts and possible steps, without claiming maturity or a fixed sequence.
description.zh: 理解表达、回应与修复三方向并列：核对双方说过什么、是否愿意继续与可选步骤；不以次数判断成熟或固定反应顺序。

All co-leaders are retained without using question order, codes or option position as a tiebreaker. The result establishes no complex personality, multiple identity or automatic way of combining the responses.
scoreReading.zh: 本次 24 题里，清楚表达、留意回应、参与分歧修复被选中的次数完全相同，且都高于调节靠近与空间。系统保留全部并列，题号、代码、选项位置都不参与排序。这不表示多重人格或身份分裂——只是这次题组里没有哪个方向明显领先。

title.en: What each tied count comes from

paragraphs.en: Clear Expression: Counts come from selecting statements that put observations, feelings, needs, views or arrangements into words. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚表达：你的清楚表达次数，来自把看法说完整、重新说明原意、提出清楚问题的题目；三个方向并列时，它和另外两个次数相同。

paragraphs.en: Attuned Response: Counts come from selecting listening, checking a meaning, asking about willingness or noticing what remains unheard. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 留意回应：你的留意回应次数，来自留意没被听见的话、先理解具体感受、问还有什么补充的题目；它在这组并列里与其余两个方向一样多。

paragraphs.en: Repair Engagement: Counts come from selecting a possible next step, discussing an impact or considering how to resume a discussion. Here this direction shares the highest count.
paragraphs.zh: 参与分歧修复：你的参与修复次数，来自寻找下一步、约定继续处理的步骤、确认弥补方式的题目；它在这组并列里与其余两个方向打了平手。

paragraphs.en: In a recent disagreement, where did explaining a view, listening and finding a next step each appear?
paragraphs.zh: 最近一次分歧里，你说清立场、听对方、找下一步的时刻分别出现在哪里？

paragraphs.en: After a misunderstanding, did you clarify meaning, try to understand or propose repair first? Check the episode rather than this tie.
paragraphs.zh: 误解发生后，你的顺序是先澄清、先理解，还是先修复？

paragraphs.en: After an argument ended, did you explain further, ask what remained unsaid or arrange another discussion?
paragraphs.zh: 争执结束后，你是把话说透、问补充，还是约复盘？

paragraphs.en: At the start of disagreement, did you finish your view, hear the other person or look for a way forward?
paragraphs.zh: 分歧刚出现时，你更常把看法说完、先听对方，还是先找路径？

paragraphs.en: Which events seemed suitable for handling then, and which required stopping first? Some situations rule out continued discussion.
paragraphs.zh: 哪些分歧适合当场处理，哪些适合先停再谈？

paragraphs.en: While explaining, did you also check what the other person actually heard?
paragraphs.zh: 你说得清楚时，有没有同时核对对方听进去了？

paragraphs.en: Have you worked hard on a repair attempt while not leaving space to hear the other person’s account?
paragraphs.zh: 有没有一次你修复得很用力，却跳过了倾听？

title.zh: 压力下的顺序需要另行观察

paragraphs.en: The equal counts cannot identify which direction appears first, takes over or switches automatically under pressure. This bank did not measure a sequence or predict your reaction to stress.
paragraphs.zh: 本次并列不能说明压力下这三个方向哪个先出现、占上风或自动切换；题组没有测量这种顺序。

paragraphs.en: In a pressured disagreement, did speaking, listening or repair come first?
paragraphs.zh: 压力下的分歧里，你实际先做的是说、听还是修？

paragraphs.en: How serious was the event, and what did each person say about their capacity or wishes?
paragraphs.zh: 当时的事件严重程度和双方状态分别是什么？

paragraphs.en: Looking back, was missing information, listening, action or something else most relevant?
paragraphs.zh: 事后看，那次缺的是内容、倾听还是行动？

title.zh: 空间与继续讨论的意愿

paragraphs.en: Before a repair proposal, did you check whether the person had finished what they wanted to say?
paragraphs.zh: 修复之前，你会先确认对方的话都说完了吗？

paragraphs.en: If discussion was not wanted, could you leave the proposed next step unpursued?
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方并不想谈，你还能忍住不推进吗？

paragraphs.en: Review a conversation where an explanation was heard and an agreed next step followed. Identify the actual feedback at each point.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你把话说清、对方听进去、后来修复成功的对话。

paragraphs.en: Compare a conversation where explaining without listening did not address the difficulty. Avoid assigning a single cause without enough information.
paragraphs.zh: 找一次你只说不听、修复失败的对话，核对缺了哪一环。

title.en: Optional actions, not a required sequence
title.zh: 可选小步骤，不规定顺序

paragraphs.en: If both people want to continue, consider making room for your own account, theirs and only then any agreed next step. This is a possible draft, not a required order.
paragraphs.zh: 下次分歧里，先说完自己的部分，再核对对方，最后才约下一步。

paragraphs.en: Before moving directly to repair, ask whether there is more the other person wants heard.
paragraphs.zh: 下次想直接进入修复前，先问：对方的话都说完了吗？

paragraphs.en: Privately record the sequence from one episode. Notice where effort went without treating ease as proof of relationship skill.
paragraphs.zh: 结束后按时间顺序写下三种先手，看哪一步最省力。

paragraphs.en: Which choices drew you toward explaining, listening and repair?
paragraphs.zh: 这次作答里，说、听、修三组题目各把你带向哪种反应？

paragraphs.en: If a disagreement involved safety or a serious principle, would a repair proposal be appropriate?
paragraphs.zh: 如果分歧涉及原则或安全，你还会继续找修复点吗？

paragraphs.en: Recall assuming responsibility for someone else’s conduct. What part was actually yours?
paragraphs.zh: 回忆一次你替对方承担了责任的分歧，那件事本该谁负责？

title.en: Read the count within its limits

paragraphs.en: These equal counts do not establish a fixed love personality.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示这三种方式组成了固定的恋爱人格。

paragraphs.en: They do not establish greater maturity or skill at maintaining relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示你更会经营关系或更成熟。

paragraphs.en: They do not mean all disagreements are solvable through conversation or that every relationship should continue.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示所有分歧都能靠沟通解决，也不表示关系必须修复。

paragraphs.en: They reveal no other person’s feelings or opinion of you.
paragraphs.zh: 不表示对方对你的感受或评价。

paragraphs.en: They predict neither compatibility nor relationship duration.
paragraphs.zh: 不预测关系会不会长久或适配。

paragraphs.zh: 试着在一次冲突里，把说清、暂停、修复各用一次。

paragraphs.zh: 结束后对比：哪种顺序让双方都更轻松。

paragraphs.zh: 如果对方需要的是当场谈，你能放下暂停的习惯吗？
